head: 542d29be994164ab0a8dc5ba2860a58106bd64c5
claim: an app can decide on a MiniMax API key through the MiniMax decide backend, and one live MiniMax-M3.1-Flash call answered a question through it

steps.start: A consumer app holds a MiniMax API key in a file and a typed intent question
steps: The app builds minimax({ model: 'MiniMax-M3.1-Flash', key }) and calls decide with a 90 s timeout
MiniMax answers over the minimax:key route (Anthropic Messages wire)
The stub test confirms the same backend through { backend: 'minimax' } config
steps.result: decide returned answer 'task' with confidence 0.85 and token usage, by minimax; the stub test passes

verdicts.seen: I read one capture entry, the MiniMax decide response. It shows "model":"MiniMax-M3.1-Flash", "by":"minimax", a "decisions" tool call with "pick":"task" and probabilities task 0.85, and "base_resp":{"status_code":0}, with usage tokens recorded. That matches the outcome: a live MiniMax-M3.1-Flash call returned a decision through the decide backend. The outcome names only one part, so parts and covers are empty. Nothing in the capture contradicts the outcome.
